title: Edge cache invalidation workbench — idea pad
content:
Quick notes / brain dump: Edge Cache Invalidation Workbench

Purpose / problem:
- Customers running Redwood Private / Dedicated want low-latency responses via local caches (edge nodes, regional proxies, client-side caches) but often need deterministic ways to invalidate or version cached outputs when model variants, prompt templates, or regulated data change.
- Current approach: ad-hoc TTLs, manual cache clear commands in infra, or re-deploy model variants -> fragile and error-prone for product teams.
- Need a lightweight, user-friendly tool for developers and SREs to define invalidation rules, preview impact, and safely roll invalidations across environments.

High-level goals:
- Provide first-class primitives for invalidation: by key, by tag/label, by model-version, by prompt-hash, by user-segment, by route.
- Let teams preview affected cache hit-rate and token-cost delta before applying broad invalidations.
- Support both push invalidations (API/console) and soft strategies (staged TTL override, canary invalidation).
- Integrate with telemetry + rollbacks: automatic snapshot of hits/misses; one-click rollback of last invalidation batch.
- Work across deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private) but start with Dedicated/Private which have more control over edge caches.

Persona(s):
- Platform engineer at customer (wants to enforce model update across caches with minimal churn).
- Product engineer shipping new prompt templates (needs to flush stale outputs causing hallucinations).
- Redwood SRE (needs guardrails to prevent accidental full-pop invalidations).
- Developer-experience engineer at Redwood (wants to instrument and ship easy SDKs).

Core features (MVP candidate):
1) Rules editor (UI + API)
   - Create rule: selector (route/model/prompt-tag/prefix), scope (edge group / region / all), action (invalidate, mark-stale -> TTL), priority, scheduled time.
   - Quick templates: "invalidate-by-model", "invalidate-by-prompt-template", "invalidate-by-route-and-version"
2) Dry-run / impact preview
   - Simulate rule over last N hours of telemetry: estimate keys affected, % of cache hits impacted, estimated token-cost delta if misses occur.
   - Visualization: small histogram of request volume vs keys touched.
3) Safe rollout modes
   - Immediate, staged (percent of edge nodes), canary (single region), time-windowed (apply at low-traffic hours).
   - Abort-if (e.g., if error-rate > X or latency increases > Y).
4) Audit + rollback
   - Every invalidation creates an immutable event with metadata (who, why, linked PR/Jira).
   - One-click rollback: re-apply previously saved cache snapshot markers or toggles TTL back.
5) API + CLI
   - Invalidate API: POST /v1/edge/invalidate { selector, scope, mode, dry_run: true }
   - CLI: rw edge invalidate --model v1.2 --scope region:us-west --staged 20%
6) SDK helpers (py/ts)
   - Helpers to compute prompt-hash, attach tags to responses at serve-time, and emit cache-key metadata.
7) Guardrails
   - Rate limits on invalidations (per-org), mandatory dry-run for >X% scope, confirmation modal for >Y keys.

UX sketches / flow (notes):
- Landing: "Active rules" + "Run new invalidation" button.
- New invalidation wizard: 1) Select selector type 2) Scope 3) Dry-run 4) Rollout mode 5) Confirm + schedule.
- Dry-run page: shows affected routes, sample keys, estimated delta in token usage, and a timeline of when it would propagate.
- Post-action: show job id, progress (per-edge node), telemetry spikes flagged, and rollback button.

User stories (rough):
- As a platform engineer, I want to invalidate cached outputs for model v1.7 across our EU edges so that newly deployed model updates are served everywhere within 30 minutes, without causing a blast of errors.
- As a PM, I want to preview how many cached entries a purge will touch so I can estimate cost and decide whether to do a staged rollout.
- As an SRE, I want automatic abort conditions on invalidation jobs if error-rate or latency crosses thresholds during rollout.
- As a developer, I want a CLI to attach provenance tags to outputs so I can later invalidate by that tag when template changes ship.

Telemetry / data we need to support dry-run and safety checks:
- Key-level request counts (last 7/30 days) per route/model/prompt-tag.
- Cache hit/miss timelines and average latency per node.
- Token cost estimate per request (or average tokens) to project cost delta.
- Edge node membership & region mapping (for staged rollout).
- Historical invalidation jobs and outcomes.

Backend design outline (short):
- Metadata store: index keys -> tags/model/version/route and last-seen timestamp. Could be a small Redis/Scylla-backed index per edge cluster.
- Invalidation coordinator: job scheduler that sends invalidation commands to edge node agents or control plane. Needs idempotency and progress tracking.
- Telemetry aggregator: reuse existing metrics pipeline but index by key/tag to allow quick estimation queries (precompute hourly aggregates?).
- Soft-invalidation mechanism: edges support setting per-key "stale-until" flag rather than full delete to allow graceful depletion.

Risks / constraints:
- Indexing every key with metadata may be expensive for high-cardinality workloads. Need sampled or tag-first approach.
- Hard invalidations can cause traffic storms; must bake in autoscaling playbooks and circuit-breakers.
- In private/on-prem customers, access to the edge nodes may be restricted — will need agent-based design or an ops-runbook.
- Legal/compliance: invalidation that touches PII may need audited confirmation. Add required fields for reason and linked ticket.

Open questions / decisions:
- Do we require every cached output to have tags at write-time? If not, how to detect which keys map to a given prompt change?
- TTL vs delete: prefer soft TTL updates by default?
- Storage for metadata: centralized vs per-edge replicated index (tradeoff latency vs consistency).
- Minimum safe limits for auto-abort thresholds — default values?

Metrics for MVP success:
- Reduction in manual cache-related incidents (qualitative).
- % of invalidations done via Workbench vs ad-hoc infra ops (target 60% first 6 months).
- Median time-to-global-invalidation for staged mode (target < 40 mins for typical sizes).
- Number of rollbacks and false-positive aborts (monitor).

Roadmap (very rough):
- Sprint 1 (2w): Proto API + CLI for scoped invalidate-by-model + dry-run engine (estimate using sample telemetry).
- Sprint 2 (3w): UI wizard + staged rollout + basic telemetry visualization.
- Sprint 3 (3w): Integrate with edge agents for progress tracking + rollback support + guardrails.
- Sprint 4 (4w): Private/Dedicated agent packaging + runbook + docs + SDK helpers.

Quick TODOs (me / follow-ups):
- Talk to telemetry team: how expensive is per-key aggregation? what's the best estimator for dry-run? (Noah)
- Ask platform PM: what are top-3 invalidation causes from customers last year? link to support tickets. (Maya)
- Prototype a small TTL-overlay mechanism in local dev to test rollout behaviour.
- Draft sample CLI UX for immediate review and put in github PR template.

Notes to self (random):
- Could combine with "model-version pinning" so invalidation is a natural part of rollouts: e.g., when new model deployed, offer to invalidate by old model tag.
- Consider "lazy invalidation" marker where a stale key is served once with a header warning and revalidation triggered for heavy hitters. Potentially less blast pressure.
- Find 1-2 pilot customers (internal Redwood demo + 1 external partner) to test the canary flows.

End of pad. Keep this lightweight. Will iterate after first sync with telemetry and platform PMs.
